title: Adiabatic perturbation theory of energy transfer and charge transport in condensed matter
abstract: Energy and charge transfer in condensed matter systems are often described in terms of quasiparticles. The order of accuracy of the results in terms of the electron-to-nucleus mass ratio $ε$, an adiabatic small parameter, is usually not known. To quantify energy transfer with controlled accuracy in $ε$, we use adiabatic perturbation theory to derive a formula for the rate of change of the nuclear kinetic energy. Applying a sequence of near-identity unitary transformations decouples the electronic and nuclear degrees of freedom to higher and higher order and produces an effective Hamiltonian. In the special case that the nuclei are treated classically, the energy transfer formula reduces to the usual formula for the rate of work done on a classical particle but the mass of the particle is enhanced by the factor $M_0^{-1}(M_0+εM_1)$, where $M_1$ is a nonadiabatic correction to the bare nuclear mass tensor $M_0$. Additional quantum geometric corrections appear at higher orders. Adiabatic perturbation theory is further used to incorporate, order-by-order in $ε$, nonadiabatic transitions into linear response calculations. The nonadiabatic frequency-dependent conductivity and Drude weight of an electron-ion system are calculated.
summary: This paper introduces Adiabatic Perturbation Theory (APT) to accurately model energy and charge transfer in electron-ion systems. It systematically derives corrections beyond the standard Born-Oppenheimer approximation by treating the small parameter $\epsilon$ (electron-to-nucleus mass ratio) perturbatively. The resulting framework allows for calculating advanced transport properties like nonadiabatic conductivity with controlled accuracy.
main_problem: The core problem is quantifying energy transfer and charge transport in condensed matter systems with controlled accuracy concerning the adiabatic small parameter ($\epsilon$, the electron-to-nucleus mass ratio). This requires going beyond standard approximations like the harmonic approximation.
main_result: The authors develop Adiabatic Perturbation Theory (APT) to systematically derive effective Hamiltonians and calculate nonadiabatic corrections to transport properties, such as frequency-dependent conductivity and Drude weight, to any desired order in $\epsilon$.
method: The primary method is Adiabatic Perturbation Theory (APT), which treats the electron-ion Schrödinger equation as a singularly perturbed differential equation in $\epsilon$ by employing near-identity unitary transformations to decouple electronic and nuclear degrees of freedom.
model_or_system: The model is an electron-ion system described by a full nonrelativistic Hamiltonian. The theory analyzes how coupling between fast electronic motion and slow, heavy ionic motion (nuclei) affects transport properties.
key_observables: Rate of change of the nuclear kinetic energy (energy transfer formula), nonadiabatic frequency-dependent conductivity, and Drude weight.
important_parameters: The adiabatic small parameter $\epsilon$ (electron-to-nucleus mass ratio); the bare nuclear mass tensor $M_0$.
main_assumptions: The theory systematically improves upon approximations by controlling errors in powers of $\epsilon$, avoiding assumptions inherent to the harmonic approximation or standard Born-Oppenheimer treatments.
paper_structure: The paper builds from identifying the failure points of simpler models (like the Harmonic Approximation) to introducing APT as a systematic, order-by-order expansion in $\epsilon$ via unitary transformations to derive an effective Hamiltonian for transport calculations.
why_interesting: This work provides rigorous, high-order theoretical tools for treating nonadiabatic coupling effects in condensed matter systems, which is crucial for understanding energy and charge flow where electronic and nuclear motions are strongly coupled.
